title: Vayishlach: three ways to prepare
hookLine: Rashi: Jacob readied gifts, prayer and defense before meeting Esau
last: TOO SMALL FOR ALL THIS KINDNESS.

cards: The night before the big interview. The surgery. The hard talk with your landlord, or your father.
Some people only worry. Some only pray. Some only make spreadsheets.

Jacob has a brother coming toward him with four hundred men, and one night to get ready. Read the chapter closely and he does three very different things. Rashi, centuries later, gave the pattern a name.

teach.b: Rashi says Jacob prepared himself for three things: for a gift, for prayer, and for war. Take them one at a time. War, or really, defense.
Jacob divides his people and flocks into two camps. If Esau attacks one, the other can escape. He isn't planning to fight his brother.
He's planning so that not everyone is lost. Prayer: we heard it yesterday. God of my fathers, I'm too small for all your kindness; save me, I'm afraid.
And a gift. Jacob sets aside hundreds of animals: goats and sheep, rams, camels with their young, cows and bulls, donkeys.
He sends them ahead in separate droves, each with its own servant, and tells them: put space between one drove and the next.

teach.h: MINCHAH: A GIFT, AND A PRAYER.
teach.b: So Esau meets gift after gift after gift, each servant saying, this is a present for my lord Esau, from your servant Jacob. The Hebrew for the gift is minchah, the same word as the afternoon prayer, Mincha.
A gift to a brother and a gift to God share a name. Jacob explains his plan in a phrase that's hard to translate. Literally: I will cover his face with the gift.
Some hear in it the root of kapparah, atonement, the covering-over of a wrong. Read that way, Jacob isn't only buying safety. He's trying to repay, a little, what he took twenty years ago.
Teachers draw a lesson from Rashi's three: facing something hard, you don't have to pick just one. Generosity, prayer for those who pray, and plain good sense can work together.

how: Jewish teachers cite Rashi's three preparations, gift, prayer and defense, as a guide for facing conflict, and the chapter is read each late autumn in Vayishlach.

games.why: Rashi says Jacob prepared three ways: a gift, prayer, and defense, splitting his camp so some could escape.

practice: Hold one hard thing coming up this week, and find one sensible step you could take, and one gift or kind word you could offer the other person.
Then, if you pray, bring it to God; if you don't, take one quiet breath with it, and let all three sit together.
